content: Cobicistat is known to interact with various drugs by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. These interactions can lead to either an increase or decrease in the levels or effects of the co-administered drugs. Below are the specific interactions and recommendations for clinical management: 1. Cabozantinib: Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the cabozantinib dose by 40 mg/day (Cometriq) or 20 mg/day (Cabometyx). Resume the original dose 2–3 days after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor. 2. Capivasertib: Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If co-administration is necessary, reduce the capivasertib dose and monitor for adverse effects. 3. Carbamazepine: This drug decreases cobicistat levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If co-administration is necessary, monitor for reduced virologic response. 4. Ceritinib: Co-administration may increase toxicity due to CYP3A4 metabolism effects. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Monitor for QT prolongation. 5. Chloramphenicol: Increases cobicistat levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 6. Clarithromycin: Both drugs increase each other's levels through CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 7. Copanlisib: Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the copanlisib dose to 45 mg. 8. Crizotinib: Co-administration increases crizotinib levels, potentially causing QT prolongation. If unavoidable, reduce the crizotinib dose to 250 mg once daily. 9. Dabrafenib: Cobicistat increases dabrafenib levels, while dabrafenib decreases cobicistat levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 10. Daridorexant: Cobicistat increases daridorexant levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 11. Darunavir: Both drugs increase each other's levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 12. Dexamethasone: Decreases cobicistat levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Co-administration with corticosteroids may lead to loss of therapeutic effect or resistance. 13. Dihydroergotamine (Intranasal): Cobicistat increases dihydroergotamine levels. Co-administration is contraindicated. 14. Doxorubicin: Cobicistat increases doxorubicin levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 15. Edoxaban: Cobicistat increases edoxaban levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Dose adjustments may be required. For DVT/PE treatment, reduce the dose to 30 mg once daily. No dose reduction is recommended for NVAF. 16. Efavirenz: Decreases cobicistat levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Co-administration may result in loss of therapeutic effect and resistance. 17. Elacestrant: Cobicistat increases elacestrant levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 18. Elbasvir/Grazoprevir: Cobicistat increases levels of these drugs. Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 19. Encorafenib: Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the dose to one-third of the original dose. Resume the original dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for 3–5 elimination half-lives. 20. Entrectinib: Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Resume the original dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for 3–5 elimination half-lives. 21. Enzalutamide: Cobicistat increases enzalutamide levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 22. Erdafitinib: Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If unavoidable, monitor closely for adverse reactions and consider dose adjustments. 23. Erythromycin (Base, Ethylsuccinate, Lactobionate, Stearate): Both drugs increase each other's levels. Avoid or use alternative antibiotics. 24. Eslicarbazepine Acetate: Decreases cobicistat levels. Avoid or use alternative anticonvulsants or antiretroviral therapy. Monitor for virologic response if co-administration is necessary. 25. Eszopiclone: Cobicistat increases eszopiclone levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 26. Etravirine: Decreases cobicistat levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 27. Everolimus: Cobicistat increases everolimus levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 28. Fedratinib: Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the dose to 200 mg/day. Increase the dose to 300 mg/day for 2 weeks, then 400 mg/day as tolerated after discontinuing the inhibitor. 29. Felbamate: Cobicistat increases felbamate levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 30. Fentanyl (Transdermal, Transmucosal): Cobicistat increases fentanyl levels. Monitor for respiratory depression and sedation. Adjust the fentanyl dose as needed. 31. Fexinidazole: Cobicistat decreases fexinidazole levels, while fexinidazole increases cobicistat levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 32. Fidaxomicin: Both drugs increase each other's levels. Avoid or use alternative antibiotics. 33. Flutamide: Cobicistat increases flutamide levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 34. Fosaprepitant: Cobicistat increases fosaprepitant levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 35. Fosphenytoin: Decreases cobicistat levels. Co-administration is contraindicated. 36. Futibatinib: Cobicistat increases futibatinib levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 37. Gilteritinib: Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If unavoidable, monitor for adverse effects and adjust the dose as needed. 38. Glasdegib: Cobicistat increases glasdegib levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Monitor for QTc prolongation. 39. Guanfacine: Cobicistat increases guanfacine levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 40. Ibrutinib: Cobicistat increases ibrutinib levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 41. Idelalisib: Both drugs increase each other's levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 42. Indinavir: Increases cobicistat levels. Co-administration is contraindicated. 43. Infigratinib: Cobicistat increases infigratinib levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 44. Itraconazole: Increases cobicistat levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 45. Ivosidenib: Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the dose to 250 mg daily. Resume the original dose after discontinuing the inhibitor for at least 5 half-lives. 46. Ixabepilone: Cobicistat increases ixabepilone levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 47. Ketoconazole: Increases cobicistat levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 48. Lapatinib: Cobicistat increases lapatinib levels. If unavoidable, administer 500 mg once daily and adjust the dose after discontinuing cobicistat. 49. Larotrectinib: Cobicistat increases larotrectinib levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 50. Lefamulin: Avoid co-administration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 51. Lemborexant: Avoid co-administration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 52. Leniolisib: Cobicistat increases leniolisib levels. Avoid or use alternative drugs.
